Fix BigBird block-sparse decoding with a KV cache (#49984)

* Fix BigBird crash with static cache / compiled generate

BigBird with block-sparse attention crashes when generating with a static cache:

    ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)

When the cache is compileable, `generate` builds the attention mask through
`create_masks_for_generate`, which returns a 4D mask. Block-sparse attention
expects a 2D mask whose length matches the input, so unpacking it fails in
`BigBirdModel.forward`.

unchanged. The full-attention path is unaffected because it builds its own 4D
mask inside the model.

Block-sparse attention never writes the prompt to the cache, so decoding
ignored the prompt and a static cache crashed. It is also bidirectional, so
its keys/values cannot be cached for causal decoding. Reuse the existing
original_full fallback instead, and drop the create_masks_for_generate
override, which is no longer needed.

🚨 Slim down `[audio]` to torchaudio + soundfile + soxr (drop librosa and phonemizer) (#50610)

* Remove librosa from the core audio loading path

load_audio gets a "soundfile" backend (soundfile decode + soxr_hq resample +
librosa's length fix) that is bit-exact with librosa.load; "auto" falls back
to it when torchcodec is unavailable. backend="librosa" becomes a deprecated
alias (FutureWarning). soxr is imported behind is_soxr_available
instead of piggybacking on librosa.

Serving, load_audio_as and nemotron_h_omni now go through load_audio; the
any_to_any librosa gate is removed; docs and docstrings use load_audio instead
of librosa.load.

librosa leaves the `[audio]` extra, replaced by what the new path uses:
soundfile>=0.13.0 and soxr>=0.5.0 (both previously pulled in only
transitively through librosa). librosa moves to `[testing]` as the reference
implementation in audio tests, so `[dev]` and CI keep it.

Floors: soundfile>=0.13.0 (first Linux aarch64 wheels, bundled libsndfile
with MP3) and soxr>=0.5.0 (first cp312-abi3 wheel, covers 3.12-3.14): every
supported platform gets wheels, nothing compiles.

* Compute parakeet / cohere_asr / nemotron_asr_streaming mel filters without librosa

These three feature extractors only needed librosa for
`librosa.filters.mel(norm="slaney")` (the `mel_filter_bank` TODO: it works
in float64, librosa rounds each band to float32). Build the filters
natively with librosa's rounding order in a `_slaney_mel_filters` method
(parakeet, inherited by nemotron_asr_streaming through modular, and the
same lines in cohere_asr, which already duplicated the librosa call), so
they no longer require librosa and the slimmer `[audio]` doesn't depend
on the AudioProcessor refactor.

filters with `librosa.filters.mel` over sr in {8k, 16k, 44.1k}, n_fft in
{256, 512, 1024}, n_mels in {64, 80, 128}, plus each default config.

* Slim down the `[audio]` extra to torchaudio + soundfile + soxr

`[audio]` now holds what the core audio path needs and nothing else:

soxr (resampling for `load_audio` and the numpy backend). phonemizer moves

Fix flaky `test_causal_lm_loss_honors_shift_labels` (#50533)

* Fix flaky `test_causal_lm_loss_honors_shift_labels`

The first check compared the loss for two random 0/1 `shift_labels`
tensors and required them to differ. On tiny random models with nearly
flat logits (e.g. Inkling, which divides its hidden states by its muP
width multiplier), the per-token loss changes have random signs and can
cancel out in the mean below float32 resolution, so the two losses are
bit-identical and the test wrongly reports that `shift_labels` is
ignored (~1 in 700-2000 runs for Inkling).

Use the most and the least likely token at every position as the two
`shift_labels` instead: every token loss then moves in the same
direction, by the max - min spread of its logits, so the mean is bound
to move.

commits.message:
[`distributed`] Trainer: reduce FSDP/HSDP gradients on the last micro-batch only (#50286)

* Reduce the gradients of FSDP/HSDP-sharded models on the last micro-batch only

The Trainer runs the non-last micro-batches of a gradient accumulation window
under `accelerator.no_sync`, which does nothing for a model sharded at load time
by `DistributedConfig`: Accelerate did not wrap it, so it reduced its gradients on
every micro-batch.

Defer the FSDP2 reduction to the last micro-batch instead. With HSDP, only the
all-reduce across replicas waits (`set_requires_all_reduce`), so the gradients stay
sharded. With FSDP, the reduce-scatter waits too (`set_requires_gradient_sync`),
like Accelerate's FSDP2 `no_sync`.

commits.message:
Keep image inputs on the first chunk of a chunked prefill (#49753)

* Keep image inputs on the first chunk of a chunked prefill

The chunked prefill called prepare_inputs_for_generation without is_first_iteration, so pixel_values and mm_encoder_outputs were dropped from every chunk and vision-language models generated without the image. The first chunk now gets is_first_iteration, as the unchunked prefill does. A Llava test checks that chunked and unchunked prefill give the same output and that the image changes it.

* Slice pre-encoded multimodal features per prefill chunk

A chunk boundary inside a run of image tokens made the model check fail, because the first chunk got the features of every image token. Each chunk now gets the rows of the pre-encoded features that belong to its own placeholder tokens, so any prefill_chunk_size matches the unchunked prefill. Models that encode raw pixel inputs inside their forward raise a clear error when the first chunk does not hold all placeholder tokens.

* Pin token_type_ids on every chunk of a chunked prefill

Gemma3 builds a bidirectional mask over each image run from token_type_ids, but only the first chunk of a chunked prefill gets them, so an image run in a later chunk attends causally and the output differs from the unchunked prefill. Strict xfail until the chunk loop passes them.

* Drop the raw multimodal input check from chunked prefill

Chunked prefill takes pre-encoded features (mm_encoder_outputs), so the branch that raised when raw placeholders crossed the first chunk is removed. _slice_mm_encoder_output reads and writes ModelOutput fields by key, which the type checker can resolve, instead of by attribute.

* Slice pre-encoded multimodal features once before the chunk loop

The per-chunk encoder outputs are built once, as a list aligned with the prefill chunks, and each chunk only looks up its entry instead of re-slicing every modality inside the loop.

* Pass token_type_ids to every chunk of a chunked prefill

token_type_ids and mm_token_type_ids are sliced per chunk like position_ids and restored after the loop. Gemma3 drops token_type_ids outside the first iteration and builds its bidirectional image mask from them by absolute position, so a later chunk gets them up to its end. is_first_iteration stays limited to chunk 0: it also selects inputs_embeds and the first-iteration mask path, so it cannot be passed to every chunk.

* Pre-build one empty dict per prefill chunk for sliced features

Each chunk starts with an empty dict that is filled per modality, and mm_encoder_outputs is passed only to chunks whose dict is non-empty, replacing the None entries and the 'or {}' fallback.

* Pass mm_token_type_ids up to the chunk end when the model drops them

Gemma4 builds its bidirectional image mask from mm_token_type_ids and drops them outside the first iteration, as Gemma3 does with token_type_ids. Each prefill chunk now gets back whichever token types the model dropped, up to the chunk end; models that keep them still get the per-chunk slice. The Gemma3 test gains a tiny Gemma4 case, which fails without this change.

* Give sliced feature tensors a single batch dim of one

Tensor features sliced for a prefill chunk are returned as (1, rows, hidden), a batch of one, instead of padding leading dims of one up to the input rank. The covered models get (1, rows, hidden) either way: Gemma3 passes a (num_images, tokens, hidden) tensor; LLaVA, Gemma4 and Qwen3-VL (pooled and deepstack) pass lists.

* Keep only pooled and deepstack features in sliced encoder outputs

The per-chunk output was a shallow copy of the whole encoder output, so each chunk held references to every hidden state and attention list. It is now a new output of the same type with only pooler_output and deepstack_features, the fields models read from pre-encoded outputs. Deepstack features in a non-tensor layout (Granite4-Vision's (layer_idx, features) pairs) are passed through as before.

* Pin per-token types on every chunk of a chunked prefill

Ernie4.5-VL-MoE routes each token by its moe_mm_token_type_ids. The chunk
loop never slices that key, so the first chunk gets the types of the whole
prompt and the MoE block fails on the shape. CTRL drops token_type_ids in
generation, and the chunk loop puts them back up to the chunk end. Both
compare chunked and unchunked generate; strict xfail until the fix lands.

* Give each prefill chunk its own token types unless the model reads them by position

The chunk loop passed token types up to the chunk end to any model that
dropped them outside the first iteration. That is right for a mask built by
absolute position (Gemma3, Gemma4, Molmo2), wrong for types read per token:
Ernie4.5-VL-MoE got the prefix on later chunks and the whole prompt's
moe_mm_token_type_ids on the first (that key was never sliced), and CTRL and
XLM, which pop token_type_ids, got them back at the prefix length.

Every chunk now gets the slice of its own tokens for every key the model
passes, moe_mm_token_type_ids included; keys the model pops stay out. A
model whose mask reads a key by position lists it in
_token_types_read_by_position, a class attribute next to _is_stateful, and
gets it from the start of the sequence. A class attribute read by _prefill is
the smallest fit: the model's own prepare_inputs_for_generation only ever
sees the chunk, so it cannot rebuild the prefix itself. Molmo2 builds the
same block mask by position and was getting the chunk slice; it is listed too.
The Ernie test now routes by type in both layers, so a wrong route on a later
chunk reaches the scores through the cache.

* Let prepare_inputs_for_generation pick the token types of each prefill chunk

The class attribute that told _prefill which token types a model reads by
position is gone, and _prefill no longer rewrites the model inputs after
prepare_inputs_for_generation. It now hands each chunk the token types up
to the chunk end, the way it already hands over the attention mask.

The generic prepare_inputs_for_generation puts token_type_ids,
mm_token_type_ids and moe_mm_token_type_ids into the model inputs and
slices them to the chunk with its existing rule for inputs that must match
input_ids. Gemma3, Gemma4, Gemma4Unified and Molmo2 build a block mask by
absolute position, so their own prepare_inputs_for_generation keeps the
types from the start of the sequence. Models that pop the key (CTRL, XLM)
still pop it.

Every chunk is now called with is_first_iteration, so models that drop
their types or switch to decoding inputs outside the first iteration treat
every chunk as prefill. Raw multimodal inputs go to the first chunk only:
models that do not pre-encode them would otherwise encode them again on
every chunk and fail to match the features to the chunk's placeholders.

* Pass Molmo2 the full token types only in prefill

Molmo2 reads mm_token_type_ids only in prefill: the forward builds the
block mask only when is_prefill, and create_masks_for_generate only when
more than one token is processed. Gate the override like Gemma3's, so
decoding steps keep what the generic method gives; Molmo2 ignores them
there, as it did on main.

* Raise on raw multimodal inputs in a split prefill; no Molmo2 types while decoding

Raw pixel or audio inputs cannot be cut into per-chunk pieces, so a model that
does not pre-encode them would either encode them again on every chunk or see
them on the first chunk only with placeholders spread over later chunks.
Instead of holding them back for the first chunk, `_prefill` now raises when
the prefill is split into more than one chunk and such inputs are present.
Pre-encoded `mm_encoder_outputs` are still split per chunk, and a prefill that
fits in one chunk behaves as without chunking.

Molmo2 now sets `mm_token_type_ids` to None outside prefill, as Gemma3 does.

* Forward Molmo2's image_num_crops like any other kwarg

Molmo2's processor returns `image_num_crops`, but pre-encoding the image does
not consume it and Molmo2's forward accepts it without reading it. As a raw
multimodal input it made every split prefill of a Molmo2 image prompt raise,
although the image itself is pre-encoded and split per chunk. Molmo2 is the
only model that uses the key.

Fix model_input_names singleton issue causing shared state (#42051)

* Fix model_input_names singleton issue causing shared state

Fixes #42024

The model_input_names attribute was defined as a class-level list, and
when initializing tokenizer instances, they were all pointing to the same
list object. This meant modifying model_input_names on one instance would
affect all other instances.

The issue was in tokenization_utils_base.py line 1417:
```python
self.model_input_names = kwargs.pop("model_input_names", self.model_input_names)
```

When no model_input_names is passed in kwargs, it would use the class
attribute directly (self.model_input_names), creating a reference to the
shared list instead of creating a new list for the instance.

Fixed by wrapping it in list() to ensure each instance gets its own copy:
```python
self.model_input_names = list(kwargs.pop("model_input_names", self.model_input_names))
```

This is a standard pattern for handling mutable default values in Python.

  dotted-path strings so the dict construction itself triggers no imports

  `_resolve_impl()`
- Add module-level `__getattr__` for backward-compatible attribute access
  (e.g. `from transformers.pipelines import TextClassificationPipeline`)

Impact (measured with the fetcher-recording recorder):
- Model test collection: 0 pipeline files loaded (was 24 in S1, unchanged in S2)
- Model test execution with RUN_PIPELINE_TESTS=1: 6 task files (was 24)

function logic to a separate `_pipeline_impl.py` so `__init__.py` becomes a

commits.message:
deal with Nan values for aggregating loss (#50172)

* Filter NaN/Inf batches out of the eval loss when `logging_nan_inf_filter` is set

A batch without label tokens has a NaN loss: an eval set with masked samples,
or a fully masked chunk under context parallelism. One such batch made the
whole `eval_loss` NaN. `logging_nan_inf_filter` already filters non-finite
training losses, so it now also leaves non-finite batches out of the eval
loss. If no batch is finite, the loss stays NaN.

Supersedes #44257, which also used `nanmean` on the gathered training loss.
That is not needed: the filter already replaces non-finite step losses
before they are accumulated.

commits.message:
Fix `WatermarkDetector` p-value computation (#50123)

Fix WatermarkDetector p-value computation

`_compute_pval` used a closed-form approximation of the normal CDF with
its square root missing, and computed the tail as `1 - cdf`, which
cancels to exactly 0 for z >= 7.56. Use the exact upper tail
`0.5 * erfc(z / sqrt(2))` via `torch.special.erfc`, which needs no new
import and stays accurate deep into the tail.

only worked if `HF_TOKEN` was also set as an env var. In clean environments
(e.g. CI pipelines that pass the token explicitly without `hf auth login`),
it would fail with a 401 / RepositoryNotFoundError.

extractors) already forward `token` correctly. This was specific to the config
loading path.

commits.message:
[exporters] resolve @register_patch paths lazily to avoid eager model imports (#50000)

* [exporters] resolve patch paths lazily in apply_patches, not at decoration time

`@register_patch` previously called `_resolve_dotted_path` (which runs
`importlib.import_module`) at module-load time, eagerly importing ~37 model
modules the moment any exporter file was imported.  Since exporter files are
imported from `test_export.py`, and `test_export.py` is imported transitively
by every `test_modeling_*.py` file via `ModelTesterMixin → ExportTesterMixin`,
this caused ~511 test files to record spurious source dependencies on those
model modules in `tests_fetcher.py`.

Fix: store the dotted-path string in `_PATCHES` instead of the resolved
object.  `apply_patches` resolves each path just before installing the patch,
at which point the model module is already loaded anyway.  The `if obj is None`
skip logic moves to `apply_patches` via the walrus operator.  `patch_attributes`
and any direct `patch_attributes(config_patches)` call-sites are unaffected.

commits.reason: Introduces bool mask for logits_to_keep in ForXXX classes.
commits.message:
logits_to_keep bool mask for all ForXXX classes (#48825)

* feat(gemma4): bool mask logits_to_keep, expose last_hidden_state

logits_to_keep only supported an int (keep the last N) or a flat
index tensor for a single packed sequence. SFT training with
sequence packing needs to exclude non-contiguous spans per example
in a batch, which neither form can express.

Accept a 2D bool mask shaped like input_ids (batch_size,
sequence_length); logits are computed only for the True positions,
flattened in input_ids order. Existing int/tensor behavior is
unchanged.

Also add last_hidden_state to Gemma4CausalLMOutputWithPast,
independent of output_hidden_states, since packed-sequence loss
computation needs the full hidden states regardless of that flag.

Closes #48784

* feat(gemma4): extend logits_to_keep mask support to all ForXXX classes, fix negative layer indices

Extend the bool-mask logits_to_keep support added for
Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration to the rest of the family
(Gemma4ForCausalLM, Gemma4UnifiedForCausalLM,
Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration), settling on a plain if/else
with a single lm_head call per branch to match the convention already
used elsewhere in the codebase (Gemma4ForCausalLM itself, biogpt, csm,
llava_onevision, etc.).

Also fix output_hidden_states selective layer capture
(src/transformers/utils/output_capturing.py, #48081) to resolve
negative indices (e.g. -1 for the last layer). The hook fires
progressively during the forward pass and can't know the total layer
count in advance, so count how many hidden_states hooks get installed
per model during the one-time hook installation walk, store it on the
model, and resolve negative indices against that count before the
forward pass runs. No change to the per-layer hook logic itself.

Refs #48784

commits.reason: Fixes silent failure in CLVP `c_proj` residual scaled-init application.
commits.message:
Fix CLVP `c_proj` residual scaled-init silently never applied (#47478)

* Fix CLVP c_proj residual scaled-init never being applied

The GPT-2 depth-scaling of residual-projection weights was gated in
_init_weights on `isinstance(module, ClvpForCausalLM)` and then an exact
parameter-name check `name == "c_proj.weight"`. Because named_parameters()
yields fully-qualified dotted names (e.g. model.decoder.layers.0.mlp.c_proj.weight),
that check never matched, so c_proj kept the default 0.02 init instead of
initializer_range / sqrt(2 * num_hidden_layers).

Apply the scaling on the concrete ClvpDecoderMLP module that owns c_proj,
mirroring the GPT-2 fix. Resolve the decoder sub-config since self.config is
the composite ClvpConfig when the full model is initialized (referencing
num_hidden_layers/initializer_range on it directly would otherwise raise).

Same root cause as the GPT-2 bug in #47458.

* Address review: drop flaky init test and trim comment

Per maintainer feedback on #47478: remove the expected-value-of-random-init test (can become flaky in CI) and trim the c_proj scaled-init comment to mirror the GPT-2 fix in #47459.

commits.reason: Guards dtype cast in TimesFM 2.5 ResidualBlock to prevent silent truncation with quantized weights.
commits.message:
Fix dtype cast in TimesFM 2.5 ResidualBlock for quantized weights (#46942)

* Guard dtype cast in TimesFM 2.5 ResidualBlock for quantized weights

`TimesFm2_5ResidualBlock.forward` casts its (float) input to
`self.input_layer.weight.dtype`. Under bitsandbytes 4/8-bit quantization
that weight dtype is an integer type (e.g. uint8), so the cast silently
truncates the float inputs to zeros (0.73 -> 0), producing garbage
outputs with no error or warning. This block is used as the model's input
projection (`input_ff_layer`), so the raw time-series inputs are affected.

Only cast when the weight dtype is floating point, matching the fix
already applied to gemma4_unified (#46904) and gemma4 (#46933).

* Test residual block input dtype

files (the original commit hand-edited them directly; this corrects that too).
